u01-open.resolution: I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'Chapter 1, verses 16 and 17' is right by content: Πῦρ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (Job 1:16) and the camels taken captive (1:17). The printed 'ι ʹ, ιζʹ' is a misprint for ιϛʹ, ιζʹ. 'Chapter 2, verse 9' introduces Χρόνου δὲ πολλοῦ προβεβηκότος, εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ, and the Greek prints Κεφ. Βʹ, θʹ before it; 'Κεφ. Ζʹ, αʹ' belongs to the following lemma. The malice clause (Ὅρα τὸ κακοῦργον …) is in the Greek. Job 12:5 LXX is ἡτοιμάσθαι πεσεῖν ὑπὸ ἄλλους εἰς χρόνον τακτόν, as quoted. 'For this is the whole of man' is the standard rendering of Eccl 12:13 τοῦτο πᾶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος. 'He' in the camels sentence is the devil, as the context makes clear. The rest (double negatives, 'I beg you', supplied copulas) is idiom.

u01-open.resolution: I found no meaning error. ἁμαρτών is the aorist participle of ἁμαρτάνω ('having sinned'), not a genitive plural noun (which would be ἁμαρτιῶν), so 'because he has sinned' is right. 'Were you formed' for ἐπάγης (πήγνυμι, 'were you fixed/established') keeps the sense of Job 15:7.
